serc_print.victim.Non Swimmer.scenario: The victim is struggling to stay above the water and is starting to panic as they cannot get to safety. They are capable of taking a rescue aid if pushed into their reach (judge will give specifics based upon scenario description). However if a contact rescue is attempted, they will struggle and try to grab hold of the rescuer (they will not turn on their back). They need assistance to get out of the water and when out will be exhausted from the experience.
serc_print.victim.Non Swimmer.notes: Non-swimmer is in imminent danger and is a high priority for rescue. They will attempt to grab any rescuer who approaches them directly without an aid. If a contact rescue is used, low marks should be recorded for the rescue component. The victim should be made safe with an effective and efficient return to safety. Landing should be done with care. They will answer questions asked of them.
serc_print.victim.Non Swimmer.criteria.a:
Recognition of non-swimmer (high priority), speed of reaching victim
Safe approach by rescuer
serc_print.victim.Non Swimmer.criteria.r:
Rescue with extreme caution
(low marks for contact rescue if not required — maximum 5 marks for this section)
Monitor while still in water; may require further directions/instructions
serc_print.victim.Non Swimmer.criteria.c:
Clear effective questioning and reassurance
Reassurance during rescue until returned to safety
serc_print.victim.Non Swimmer.criteria.l:
Care of the victim; protection of the head
Appropriate landing for size and strength of rescuer
serc_print.victim.Non Swimmer.criteria.c: Safe position away from the edge; warmth and protection where possible; monitor safety; ongoing reassurance
serc_print.victim.Weak Swimmer.scenario: The victim is a weak swimmer struggling to get back to safety. They will be capable of shouting or calling out for help. They will be able to take an aid to get to safety. If a contact carry is performed they will struggle and resist. They will be able to land themselves. They will provide assistance or contact emergency services and will cooperative throughout.
serc_print.victim.Weak Swimmer.notes: Weak swimmers need to be made safe very quickly. The victim can be talked at or given signs to return to safety; they will need to be kept monitored. They will struggle if a contact rescue is used; low marks should be awarded for contact rescue.
Recognition that they are a weak swimmer and high priority to mobilize.
Safe approach by rescuer

Encourage return to safety with clear directions; perform a non-contact rescue (low marks for contact rescue if not required — maximum 5 marks for this section)
Monitor while still in water; may require further directions/instructions
Effective communication / instruction; use for keeping another victim warm / safe

Make secure and land
Appropriate landing for size and strength of rescuer
Safe position away from danger; warmth and protection where possible; monitor safety; ongoing monitoring and care
serc_print.victim.Injured Swimmer.scenar: Victim will be complaining of a specific injury and will not be calmed.
serc_print.victim.Injured Swimmer.notes: This is a medium priority victim requiring assistance. Rescuer should use an aid. Victim may not be able to hold an aid depending on the injury and may need assistance in the water and on landing. The victim should be removed carefully from the water with attention to the injured part of the body. They will not be cooperative.
serc_print.victim.Injured Swimmer.criter:
Recognition that they are an injured swimmer and medium priority to mobilize
Safe approach by rescuer

Encourage to return to the edge with clear directions
Perform non-contact rescue
(low marks for contact rescue if not required — maximum 5 marks for this section)
Monitor while still in water; may require further directions/instructions

Effective communication / instruction
Reassurance throughout rescue

Careful removal from water with attention to injury
Make secure and land (monitor while still in water; may require further directions/instructions)
Appropriate landing for size and strength of rescuer
Safe position away from the edge; warmth and protection where possible; monitor safety; ongoing monitoring and care
serc_print.victim.Unconscious Non-Breath: This victim will be on the bottom of the pool.

This victim is a low-order rescue priority and rescuers should deal with the high priority victims as quickly as possible in order to get to this victim who requires continuous care.
CPR should be commenced when it is safe to do so; on land, boat, rescue breaths with a buoyant aid in the water, etc. and your marks should reflect the efficiency and effectiveness of the CPR simulation.

Speed of rescue (considering priority of rescue)
Speed in getting back to safety

Effective and efficient CPR likely to assist recovery
Safe position away from danger; monitor safety; ongoing monitoring and care
serc_print.overall.notes: You have the overview of the SERC area and assess overall efficiency of the team. In particular you mark the Team Leader's control of the team — assessment of priorities and dispatch/direction of team members to deal with the victims. You will also mark communication between the Leader and the team and between team members and this may include information about the condition of the victims and what help is needed. Your marks MUST take into account:
serc_print.overall.bullets.0: Any loss of control by the Leader becoming committed or involved to such an extent that overall control is lost.
serc_print.overall.bullets.1: Do not mark any rescues the leader carries out as another judge is allocated to that victim.
serc_print.overall.bullets.2: Whether assistance was sought. Any person sent for help as assistant will not be allowed to return.
serc_print.overall.criteria.assessment:
Assessment of the emergency
Did the Leader coordinate the team and direct to the correct priorities of rescue?
On-going assessment / re-assessment
serc_print.overall.criteria.control:
Control and safety over the scenario area
Leader retains control throughout the scenario
On-going assessment / re-assessment
serc_print.overall.criteria.communicatio:
Communication and feedback between Leader and team members,
And between team members and victims
Basic questioning and simple instructions given to victims and team
Note: Emphasis is on non-verbal and simple verbal communication and not on extensive verbal communication.
serc_print.overall.criteria.search:
Effective search of scenario area
Identification and location of victims
serc_print.overall.criteria.teamwork:
Teamwork, summon assistance (emergency services called) with appropriate information provided
Identification and securing of all victims
Effective use of bystanders / victims
serc_print.bystander.scenario: The bystander will not offer assistance but will be cooperative and take direction.
serc_print.bystander.notes: This is a high priority bystander as they can lend assistance when given direction.
serc_print.bystander.criteria.approach.d: Recognition that they are a bystander and cooperative.
serc_print.bystander.criteria.info.label: Assesses relevant information
serc_print.bystander.criteria.info.desc:
Questions bystander to assess information about the scenario.
(low marks for not giving the bystander directions — maximum 5 marks for this section)
serc_print.bystander.criteria.directions: Rescuer provides directions or instructions to assist the rescue scenario such as; asst. removals, reassure victims, call emergency services.
serc_print.bystander.criteria.monitoring: Check periodically to ensure that bystander has followed the directions of the Rescuer throughout rescue.
serc_print.bystander.criteria.encouragem: Provides feedback to bystander on their actions to encourage them to assist with victim support.

email.invite.org.subject: Organizing — {meet}
email.invite.org.body:
Hello,

You are invited to organize {meet} for {club}. You can start preparing the meet and inviting teams now.

{deadline}

How to proceed:

  1. Get your PIN. Click the secure link below to reveal your PIN. The link can only be used once and expires in 7 days — write the PIN down immediately, it will not be shown again.
    {secret_url}
  2. Open the portal at {base_url} and log in with your PIN.
  3. Create the meet structure (sessions, events, fees, entry deadline) in the Meet tab.
  4. Invite the teams from the Invitation tab, once the structure is ready.

Here is the organizer manual: {manual_url}

Good luck!

email.invite.team.body:
Hello,

You are invited to register the athletes of your team {club} for {meet}{organized_by}.

{deadline}

How to proceed:

  1. Get your PIN. Click the secure link below to reveal your PIN. The link can only be used once and expires in 7 days — write the PIN down immediately, it will not be shown again.
    {secret_url}
  2. Open the registration portal at {base_url} and log in with your team's PIN.
  3. Register your athletes. Pick an athlete, check the events, select the category (15-18 / Open / Masters) and adjust the entry time if needed. Repeat for every athlete you want to register.

Good luck!
quickbooks.readme:
QuickBooks Online import - {n_invoices} invoice(s) in {n_files} file(s)

1. Settings > Import data > Customers: upload 1-customers.csv.
   Skip this step for clubs that already exist as customers (QuickBooks cannot
   import a name that already exists, and the invoice must use the exact same name).
2. Make sure the product/service "{item_name}" exists (create it once, linked to
   your income account).
3. Settings > Import data > Invoices: upload each 2-invoices*.csv file, map the columns
   if asked, pick the date format dd/MM/yyyy. The tax code on every line is
   "{tax_code}": it must be the exact name of your exempt tax code.

Importing the same invoice number twice is refused or duplicated: if a club changes its
entries afterwards, correct that invoice in QuickBooks.
